doc.name: Robert Blust
doc.instructions:
Whoever asks about my work — a person, a search engine, an agent — reaches the same answer, because every surface they can reach derives from one model I keep, and no claim in it stands without its evidence.

A company of one: technology leadership and business architecture, and the models that let people and agents both work inside a business.

Terms the tools use. An id identifies one entity across the whole model and stays with it when its page moves. Every tool that takes an entity takes its id or its address, the folder and slug where its page sits, and every answer gives the id. A canonical name is an entity's title, unique within its type and, for an owned type, within its owner, so a name alone can be ambiguous where an id cannot. An owner is the entity another is nested under; the word is the tools' own, for their `owner` argument and field, and not an answer to a question: a visitor asking what an owner is asks about the model, which may hold an entity of that name, so search the model for it first. A reference is an edge from one entity to another, and `via` names the field or Section.Column that drew it, or `nested-in` for nesting, a name no schema declares. A qualifier is a value on a table row that describes that row's edge and draws none of its own. A list answers a page at a time: follow `page.nextCursor` while `page.hasMore`. A refused call carries `error.code` for a program beside the sentence for a reader, and describe_errors gives the codes and the schema of a refusal.

This server reports what the model says at one commit, which every answer names under `model`, and adds nothing.

tools.name: list_types
tools.description: Every type the model's schemas declare. Use first, to learn which types exist before listing or describing one. No input. Returns `types`, each with `type`, `name`, `tagline`, `owner` (the type it nests under, or null) and `count`, the entities it holds.

tools.name: describe_schema
tools.description: One type's schema: its sections as written and its declared relations as data. Use to learn what an entity of the type may hold; for the whole vocabulary use describe_relations. Input: `type`. Returns `url`, the schema's own file, `sections`, and `relations`: owner, owns, references both ways, enums, joins and lists.

type.description: A type name from list_types, such as skill

tools.name: describe_relations
tools.description: What the schemas declare between types: references with form and cardinality, ownership, enums, joins, list kinds. Use for a diagram or audit; for one type's full schema use describe_schema. Optional `type` narrows every list, `direction` (declares, declared-to, both; needs `type`) one side of relations, `via` relations and enums. Returns those lists, with `forms` and `reading` explaining every term. Not paged.

tools.name: list_rules
tools.description: The vocabulary's conventions the model is held to, R0 onwards, from its core's CONVENTIONS.md. Use to resolve a number a schema or refusal cites, such as R9. A company's own rules are entities of type `rule`: list_entities and get_entity. No input. Returns `tagline`, the file's `url`, and `rules`, each with `rule`, `title` and `part`; describe_rule gives one rule's text.

tools.name: describe_rule
tools.description: One convention of the vocabulary as written, not a company's own rule (an entity of type `rule`: list_entities, get_entity). Input: `rule`, a number from list_rules such as R9, in either case. Returns `rule`, `title`, `part`, `text` and the file's `url`. An unknown number is refused with the known ones listed.

rule.description: A convention's number from list_rules, such as R9

tools.name: list_checks
tools.description: The checks the model's own gate runs, from the checker release this server was built with. Use to see which rules a script enforces and which are left to a reader. No input. Returns `checks`, each with `name`, `rule`, `title` and what it `reports`, a `failure` or a `note` that fails nothing, and `ranBy`. This server runs none of them.

tools.name: describe_errors
tools.description: What a refused call looks like. A tool's output schema covers its answers only, so use this once, to branch on refusals or validate them. No input. Returns `errors`, every `code` with `when` it is raised and the JSON Schema of its `details`, and `schema`, the JSON Schema of a whole refusal: `error` with `code`, `message`, `rule`, `details`, beside `model`.

tools.name: list_entities
tools.description: Entities with their frontmatter's short facts, in address order or newest first. Use to browse, or for what runs on a date, came last or has a value; to find by words use search. Input: optional `type`, `owner`, `order`, `on`, `by`, `where`, `fields`, `limit`, `cursor`. Returns `entities` with `fields`, and `page`; follow `page.nextCursor` while `page.hasMore`.

type.description: A type, to keep its entities; leave it out to list every type

owner.description: An owner's id or address, to keep its entities

order.description: address, where the pages sit, by default; newest or oldest, by when each entity came into the model, or by the date `by` names

on.description: A date, YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD: keep the entities whose period, start to end, holds it; an absent end is still running

by.description: A date field, such as start or decided, to order by in the direction order names

where.description: Field values to keep, ignoring case, by field name; a reference matches by the name its page writes

fields.description: Fields to add by name beside the short ones every entity carries, such as an array

limit.description: Entries per page: 50 by default, clamped to 1–200, so 0 returns one entry and 1000 returns 200.

cursor.description: `page.nextCursor` from the previous answer, sent with the same arguments; omit it for the first page.

tools.name: get_entity
tools.description: One entity as structured data: fields, sections, tables, references both ways. Use to reason over one; for its page as written use fetch. Input: `id` or address, where its page sits, or `type` and `name`; an ambiguous name is refused with candidate ids. Returns `entity`, by id. Reference lists hold at most 50 edges; `referenceCounts` gives totals, list_references the rest.

id.description: The entity's id, as any answer gives it, or its address, where its page sits

name.description: The canonical name, the entity's H1; needs type

tools.name: list_references
tools.description: The model's edges, filtered and paged. Use to inspect one entity's relations or one kind of reference without taking whole entities. Optional `entity` (an id or address), `direction` (out, in, both; needs `entity`), `via`, `type` (the far end's type, or either end's without `entity`), `limit`, `cursor`. Returns `edges`, each `from`, `via`, `to`, `attrs`, and `page`.

limit.description: Entries per page: 50 by default, clamped to 1–200, so 0 returns one entry and 1000 returns 200.

cursor.description: `page.nextCursor` from the previous answer, sent with the same arguments; omit it for the first page.

tools.name: find_evidence
tools.description: Every edge into one skill, grouped by the type of the page that drew it. Use to check a claimed skill against its evidence. Input: `skill`, an id, canonical name or address; optional `limit`, `cursor`. Returns `skill`, `evidence` and `page`; a profile's claim arrives via Skills.Skill with its level, an evidence row via Evidence.Skill. Attributes are verbatim.

skill.description: The skill's id, canonical name or address

limit.description: Entries per page: 50 by default, clamped to 1–200, so 0 returns one entry and 1000 returns 200.

cursor.description: `page.nextCursor` from the previous answer, sent with the same arguments; omit it for the first page.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find entities by words, substring or exact name. `match: "words"` needs every query word's stem in name, tagline, fields, sections or cells; `"text"` (default) is a case-insensitive substring over the same; `"name"` the exact canonical name. Optional `type`, `owner`, `limit`, `cursor`. Returns `results` with `id`, `title`, `type`, `matched`, `words` in words mode, and `page`: name matches first, then a listing.

owner.description: An owner's id or address, to keep its entities

limit.description: Entries per page: 50 by default, clamped to 1–200, so 0 returns one entry and 1000 returns 200.

cursor.description: `page.nextCursor` from the previous answer, sent with the same arguments; omit it for the first page.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: One entity's page as written. Use to quote or display the source; for structured fields and references use get_entity. Input: `id` or address, from search, list_entities or any reference. Returns `id`, `title`, `type`, `url` and `text`, the Markdown source. Takes no name: search with match "name" finds the id.

tools.name: diagram
tools.description: A picture of the model as Mermaid; edge data: list_references. Input: `shape`; `id`, `domain`, `type` or `unit` narrow it. aggregate, flow, lifecycle take a context's `id`; organization without `id` draws the company; system a landscape, holds its data; usecase, scenario a use case's; requirements a feature's, product's, use case's or requirement's. Returns `mermaid`, `nodes`, `links`, `units`, counts. Max 50 nodes.

id.description: The process, the entity at a neighborhood's middle, the bounded context of a context map, or the aggregate or bounded context of an aggregate, flow or lifecycle picture, the group an organization is narrowed to, or the system drawn in its landscape by system and by the data it holds by holds, the use case drawn by usecase and scenario, or the feature, product, use case or requirement whose requirements are drawn, never by neighborhood

domain.description: A domain's id or address, to draw its concepts

type.description: A type, to draw its schema and the types it is declared with

unit.description: core or a pack, to draw that unit's types and what they declare; a meta-model too large to draw whole is drawn as core, and `units` in the answer names every unit
